q: Magnesium glycinate vs citrate: which is better?

q: Magnesium oxide vs glycinate: what's the difference?

Glycinate is only about 14% magnesium but was better absorbed than oxide in small studies and is gentler on the stomach. For daily intake, choose glycinate; for constipation, oxide is the studied option.

q: Is magnesium bisglycinate the same as magnesium glycinate?
a: Usually, yes. Both names describe magnesium bound to two molecules of the amino acid glycine (a chelate); it is sometimes called diglycinate. Labels use the names interchangeably. What matters is the elemental magnesium per serving, which the Supplement Facts panel must list.

q: Magnesium glycinate vs threonate: which should I take?

Threonate (Magtein) is marketed for the brain, based mostly on rat studies and small, often company-funded trials; one independent trial found no benefit. No study has compared them head to head.

q: How does an at-home A1c test work?

q: How accurate is an at-home vitamin D test?
